$comment: Single source for the published route roster and its quality-gate coverage (Issue #492). Read by scripts/check-route-quality-coverage.mjs, which fails when the roster derived from src/routes/** and this manifest drift apart. See docs/verification/quality/route-quality-coverage.md.

derived_from.note: A file under route_root is a route when it calls createFileRoute('<id>'). The generated route_tree must list exactly the same route ids; the `path` of an entry is the id with TanStack's nesting markers removed. Adding a route file without adding an entry here fails `pnpm run routes:quality:check`.

gate_families.contract: A Playwright spec under e2e/ opens the surface against a running Worker (local `pnpm dev`, or the deployed origin in the production smoke workflow) and asserts what it renders.

A spec asserts the canonical link plus the Open Graph / Twitter metadata the surface publishes to link unfurlers. A 200 response is not this family; robots.txt and sitemap.xml are not generated at this release and are therefore outside the contract.

An automated axe-core scan runs over the rendered surface and its violations are gated. Hand-written landmark / heading assertions in the e2e specs do not satisfy this family — they are a weaker, different check.

A Lighthouse (or equivalent) measurement of the surface exists at a recorded threshold. #384 makes the measurement reproducible, #385 makes it a release gate, #386 sets the Core Web Vitals budget; until then no surface is measured here.
The surface is exercised in at least two browser engines in CI. Today CI installs Chromium only (`pnpm run e2e:install`), so no surface has a second engine.
A spec asserts the response security headers the Worker sends for the surface (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy). A cookie flag assertion is not this family.
